items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Mr. Tailgate you mean? Yeah. I don't know what the other call is that.

ctx.x: The only thing they got new is they all entertain, they sing and everything, you know what I mean? Yeah. I was working with an orchestra, I swear to God, let me tell you the truth up north. They were traveling around the coal mines in West Virginia, all around these places. And we were only about nine men in the band. Man, that's a good job, coal mine job, man. We'd be in this little town for three nights, man, and make $75, $100, you know what I mean? A snack. Okay. And every man named- But you didn't have a…

You mean the man, somebody knocked on his door? Santo Piccolo? Somebody knocked on his head or something. I had something with me. Mr. Tailgate you mean? Yeah. I don't know what the other call is that. I had something with me. The price of fame, huh? I was in Chicago.
I'm sleeping one morning, who comes in there knocking on the door with Santa? Come on.
